spans.label: std, plonky2, serde and crate imports
spans.note: Hasher, builder and serde interfaces are imported; the model replaces them with the opaque HashEnv record.

spans.label: Hasher/HashOut/HasherFromTarget/HashOutTarget type aliases
spans.note: The associated-type projections through Leafable/LeafableHasher are collapsed into the opaque callback record; no property of the concrete Poseidon instance is established.

spans.label: doc comment and derive attribute
spans.note: No executable constraint is inferred from comments or derives.

spans.label: MerkleTree fields (height, node_hashes, zero_hashes) and impl header
spans.note: The HashMap is modelled as an association list whose insert is a prepend; lookup order is the same, memory behaviour is not modelled.

spans.label: MerkleTree::new builds zero_hashes = [H(empty_leaf), H(h,h), ...]
spans.note: Pins the height+1 zero-hash convention and the doubling recurrence; no source refinement.

spans.label: MerkleTree::height accessor
spans.note: Handwritten local semantics; no source refinement.

spans.label: get_node_hash: stored node else zero_hashes[height - path.len()]
spans.note: The Rust indexing panics when path.len() > height; Nat subtraction saturates instead, so that panic is NOT modelled.

spans.label: MerkleTree::get_root = get_node_hash(BitPath::default())
spans.note: Handwritten local semantics; no source refinement.

spans.label: update_leaf: insert the leaf hash then climb, swapping on the popped bit
spans.note: Pins the left/right discipline: a popped bit of 1 puts the running hash on the RIGHT. The index is not masked to height bits.

spans.label: MerkleTree::prove collects exactly `height` siblings, leaf level first
spans.note: Pins the height/sibling-count relation and the leaf-to-root ordering; no source refinement.

spans.label: blank line and derive attribute
spans.note: No executable constraint is inferred from derives.

spans.label: MerkleProof { siblings }
spans.note: A proof carries only its sibling vector; its height is that vector's length.

spans.label: hand-written Serialize/Deserialize for MerkleProof
spans.note: Serialization is the identity on the sibling vector in the source; the model does not cover encoding, and a decoded proof of ANY length is accepted by Deserialize.

spans.label: MerkleProof::dummy(height) = height copies of HashOut::default()
spans.note: The dummy siblings are the DEFAULT digest, not the zero-subtree hashes, so a dummy proof is not an opening of the empty tree; the 63- and 32-sibling instances used by the circuits are pinned.

spans.label: MerkleProof::height() = siblings.len()
spans.note: Handwritten local semantics; no source refinement.

spans.label: MerkleProof::get_root: hash the leaf, then fold siblings against the popped index bits
spans.note: The `path.pop().unwrap()` is shown never to fire. Recomputation is a deterministic function of (leaf hash, index bits, siblings); index bits above the sibling count are silently ignored.

spans.label: MerkleProof::verify compares the recomputed root with the supplied root
spans.note: Acceptance is exactly root equality. Binding two openings to the same leaf needs the EXPLICIT NoCollisionAlong and LeafHashInjectiveOn premises; it is not a consequence of the source.

spans.label: MerkleProofTarget struct over plonky2 HashOutTarget
spans.note: Circuit targets are modelled as an arbitrary satisfying witness record; the target representation itself is an imported interface.

spans.label: MerkleProofTarget::new / ::constant / ::set_witness
spans.note: Only the set_witness length assertion is modelled; virtual-target allocation, constant embedding and witness writing are imported builder behaviour.

spans.label: MerkleProofTarget::get_root: split_le index bits zipped with siblings, two_to_one_swapped per level
spans.note: split_le is modelled only as the range premise index < 2^height and the same little-endian bit order; the swap gate lowering is an undischarged boundary.

spans.label: MerkleProofTarget::verify (unconditional connect_hash)
spans.note: Modelled as a Prop over an ARBITRARY witness, not as the native builder path; connect_hash lowering is a boundary.

spans.label: MerkleProofTarget::conditional_verify (root recomputed always, equality gated)
spans.note: With the condition false the gadget constrains NOTHING about the claimed root; callers must supply the condition's meaning themselves.

spans.label: MerkleProofTarget::height() = siblings.len()
spans.note: The in-circuit height is likewise the sibling count, fixed at circuit-build time.

spans.label: closing brace and blank line
spans.note: No executable constraint is inferred from punctuation.

boundaries.name: poseidon-hash-callback
boundaries.obligation: Leafable::hash and LeafableHasher::two_to_one are opaque callbacks (HashEnv). Nothing here establishes collision resistance, preimage resistance, or any algebraic property of Poseidon/Keccak, nor that leaf and node hashing are domain separated (they are not).

boundaries.name: collision-freedom-premise
boundaries.obligation: NoCollisionAlong and LeafHashInjectiveOn are explicit, undischarged premises about the specific compared pairs. They are NOT global hash injectivity and are not proved for the real hash.

boundaries.name: native-target-refinement
boundaries.obligation: The Lean definitions are a handwritten local semantics. No refinement of the Rust source, of rustc codegen, or of the plonky2-compiled circuit is proved.

boundaries.name: rust-integer-widths
boundaries.obligation: BitPath.length (u32), BitPath.value (u64) and usize heights/lengths are modelled as unbounded Nat. Wrap-around of `>>=`/`^=`, `1 << height` overflow on 32-bit targets, and usize truncation are not modelled.

boundaries.name: root-provenance
boundaries.obligation: A verified opening says only that the recomputed root equals the supplied root. Nothing here establishes that the root is canonical, current, on-chain, or produced by an honest tree.

boundaries.name: plonky2-gate-lowering
boundaries.obligation: CircuitBuilder, split_le, two_to_one_swapped, connect_hash and conditional_assert_eq_hash are modelled as Props over an arbitrary witness. Gate lowering, range-check soundness of split_le, and witness-generation correctness are not proved.

boundaries.name: hashmap-semantics
boundaries.obligation: The node_hashes HashMap is modelled as a prepend-only association list; hashing of BitPath keys, capacity behaviour and iteration order are not modelled.

boundaries.name: serde-roundtrip
boundaries.obligation: MerkleProof's hand-written Serialize/Deserialize is not modelled; Deserialize accepts a sibling vector of any length, so a deserialized proof's height is attacker-chosen unless the caller checks it.

boundaries.name: index-range-divergence
boundaries.obligation: Native BitPath::new does not mask the index, so native verify accepts index + 2^height; the in-circuit split_le range check does not. Nothing here proves the two paths are used consistently by callers.

boundaries.name: native-vs-arbitrary-witness
boundaries.obligation: MerkleProofTarget is modelled as a Prop over an arbitrary satisfying witness. Theorems about the native MerkleTree::prove path do not cover adversarial witnesses, and vice versa.
